citations.title: Training BIG to move faster: the application of the speed-amplitude relation as a rehabilitation strategy for people with Parkinson's disease
citations.what_it_says: Foundational amplitude-training study by PWR!'s founder showing intensive large-amplitude whole-body movement practice reduced bradykinesia/hypokinesia in PD stages I-III.

citations.authors: Fox C, Ebersbach G, Ramig L, Sapir S
citations.title: LSVT LOUD and LSVT BIG: Behavioral Treatment Programs for Speech and Body Movement in Parkinson Disease
citations.what_it_says: Reviews the amplitude- and neuroplasticity-principled rationale extending LSVT from speech to body movement; documents the shared scientific lineage PWR! draws upon.

citations.authors: Ebersbach G, Ebersbach A, Edler D, Kaufhold O, Kusch M, Kupsch A, Wissel J
citations.title: Comparing exercise in Parkinson's disease — the Berlin LSVT BIG study
citations.what_it_says: RCT (n=60): amplitude-based BIG training improved UPDRS motor scores more than Nordic walking or unsupervised home exercise.

citations.authors: Schenkman M, Moore CG, Kohrt WM, et al.
citations.title: Effect of High-Intensity Treadmill Exercise on Motor Symptoms in Patients With De Novo Parkinson Disease: A Phase 2 Randomized Clinical Trial (SPARX)
citations.what_it_says: Phase 2 RCT (n=128): high-intensity treadmill exercise is safe and slows motor symptom worsening in de novo PD; anchors the exercise-as-medicine rationale.

citations.authors: Petzinger GM, Fisher BE, McEwen S, Beeler JA, Walsh JP, Jakowec MW
citations.title: Exercise-enhanced neuroplasticity targeting motor and cognitive circuitry in Parkinson's disease
citations.what_it_says: Influential review establishing that goal-based, cognitively engaging, skill-based exercise promotes neuroplasticity in PD circuitry; the mechanistic justification for PWR!'s training style.

citations.authors: Mak MK, Wong-Yu IS, Shen X, Chung CL
citations.title: Long-term effects of exercise and physical therapy in people with Parkinson disease
citations.what_it_says: Progressive strength and aerobic training yield gains lasting 12-24 months in PD; supports sustained, ongoing programming of the kind PWR! community classes deliver.

citations.authors: Tomlinson CL, Patel S, Meek C, et al.
citations.title: Physiotherapy versus placebo or no intervention in Parkinson's disease
citations.what_it_says: Cochrane review: short-term physiotherapy benefits for gait, balance, and mobility in PD, with effects often not durable; a balanced backdrop for PWR!'s evidence base.

citations.authors: Corcos DM, Robichaud JA, David FJ, et al.
citations.title: A two-year randomized controlled trial of progressive resistance exercise for Parkinson's disease
citations.what_it_says: Two-year RCT: progressive resistance exercise produced superior, sustained off-medication UPDRS-III improvement vs stretching/balance.

citations.title: Does vigorous exercise have a neuroprotective effect in Parkinson disease?
citations.what_it_says: Synthesizes animal and human evidence that vigorous exercise may be neuroprotective in PD via BDNF and neuroplasticity.

citations.authors: Combs SA, Diehl MD, Chrzastowski C, et al.
citations.title: Community-based group exercise for persons with Parkinson disease: a randomized controlled trial
citations.what_it_says: RCT: community-based group exercise produced large improvements in balance, mobility, and quality of life in PD; directly supports the group/community delivery model PWR! uses.
